sections.title: Synopsis
sections.text: Models indicate that a deep mid-level closed low will accelerate east southeast of the Hudson/James Bay region, toward the Canadian Maritimes during this forecast period. As it does, a belt of seasonably strong cyclonic mid/upper flow on its southern periphery appears likely to overspread northern New England by late tonight, with a significant associated cold front advancing southward through the St. Lawrence Valley and portions of the upper Great Lakes region. A more modest belt of mid-latitude westerlies may remain broadly cyclonic southeast of the lower Great Lakes through the northern Mid Atlantic coast and southern New England, but mid-level heights are forecast to rise through the day, ahead of a low amplitude wave progressing through more or less zonal flow across the northern Plains and upper Mississippi Valley. On the southern fringe of this belt of westerlies, a lingering corridor of seasonably moist conditions beneath modestly steep mid-level lapse rates (associated with a remnant plume of elevated mixed layer air) likely will support moderate to strong potential instability by late this afternoon and evening. sections.title: Upper Mississippi Valley
sections.text: Considerable variability within the model guidance exists concerning sub-synoptic scale developments across the region today, which could have a considerable impact on thunderstorm initiation and subsequent evolution. However, lower/mid tropospheric warm advection ahead of the low amplitude mid-level wave may provide the general support for the initiation of storms across the upper Mississippi Valley region by this evening, as moisture return contributes to increasing destabilization. This could include moderate CAPE, and the environment appears likely to be at least conditionally supportive of one or two upscale growing convective clusters with potential for severe hail and winds. A more precise focus for any such development remains unclear, but a general consensus of model output appears to suggest highest probabilities within a corridor from upper portions of the northern Plains Red River Valley though much of central Minnesota by this evening. ...Ohio Valley into northern Mid Atlantic Coast and southern New England... sections.title: Northern New England
sections.text: Timing of pre-frontal convective development into portions of northern Maine may not be until after dark, when modest daytime boundary layer destabilization will be in the process of waning. However, coinciding with strengthening of deep layer wind fields and shear, severe weather probabilities may not be negligible. ..Kerr/Marsh.. 07/11/2017

outlooks.summary: Severe thunderstorms are expected this afternoon into tonight especially across parts of the Upper Midwest.

sections.title: Dakotas/Upper Midwest to Lake Michigan vicinity
sections.text: A flattening belt of moderately strong progressive westerlies will overspread the region today. Embedded within this regime, multiple small-scale convectively related/enhanced disturbances will influence the region through the afternoon into tonight, with the relative subtlety of these features (and related early-day cloud cover and precipitation) complicating some of the timing and spatial details of the severe risk later today. Latest thinking is that strong/potentially severe thunderstorm development may first occur by around mid/late afternoon across parts of northern into central ND near a surface low and southward-sagging front. Although the exact timing is a bit uncertain, other at least isolated deep convective development will be possible by late afternoon and early evening across the eastern Dakotas into western MN within an increasingly unstable air mass near/just north of a surface triple point. Ample moisture and steep lapse rates will support upwards of 2500-4500 J/kg of MLCAPE, with 40+ kt effective shear being supportive of supercells capable of large hail. sections.title: Ohio Valley to Mid-Atlantic/Northeast coastal areas
sections.text: Amid a modestly strong belt of mid-level westerlies, multiple east/southeastward-moving clusters of storms and/or small-scale mid-level disturbances/MCVs are noted this morning (as of 13Z) along with semi-prevalent cloud cover from northern IL/central IN into WV. While overall forcing will generally remain subtle, outflows and/or the aforementioned mid-level perturbations should contribute to an increase in thunderstorm coverage and intensity within a relatively moist and increasingly unstable air mass this afternoon. The strongest of this activity will be capable of damaging wind gusts mainly this afternoon into evening.

sections.title: Parts of MT/northern WY to Black Hills vicinity
sections.text: Although the air mass across the region will not be overly moist or unstable, relatively strong mid-level westerlies and related 35-45 kt of deep-layer shear may support a few potentially severe high-based storms this afternoon into evening. Severe-caliber wind gusts and some hail will be possible with the stronger storms.

sections.title: Maine
sections.text: Timing of pre-frontal convective development into portions of northern Maine may not be until early evening or later, when modest daytime boundary layer destabilization will be in the process of waning. However, in the presence of strengthening of deep layer wind fields and shear, a couple of strong to locally severe thunderstorms could occur. ..Guyer/Peters.. 07/11/2017

outlooks.summary: Severe thunderstorms are expected this afternoon into tonight especially across parts of the Upper Midwest.

sections.title: Upper Midwest
sections.text: Very few changes have been made to the ongoing forecast. Models continue to indicate that strong instability will develop this afternoon across parts of eastern ND into central MN. Forecast soundings suggest that a capping inversion will inhibit convective initiation until late this afternoon, when a shortwave over western ND approaches the region and helps to break the cap. Isolated supercells will be preferred early, with upscale organization to bowing segments during the evening as storms spread across the ENH area. Large hail and damaging winds will be possible, along with an isolated tornado or two. 12z CAM solutions are inconsistent regarding the details of timing/location of the most intense storms, so have chosen not to attempt to fine-tune the ongoing forecast areas.

sections.title: IL to the Mid Atlantic Region
sections.text: Ample low-level moisture and instability along the southern fringe of stronger westerly flow will promote a risk of scattered thunderstorms this afternoon from the mid MS Valley into the Mid Atlantic Region. The potential exists for one or two organized/bowing clusters with a risk of damaging wind gusts and hail. However, forecast soundings indicate the overall threat is marginal.

sections.title: Northern Rockies and High Plains
sections.text: Scattered thunderstorms are expected to form over parts of MT this afternoon, spreading into adjacent parts of ND and WY this evening. Isolated rotating storms are possible, capable of hail and damaging wind gusts. ..Hart/Jewell.. 07/11/2017

outlooks.summary: A risk for severe thunderstorms continues this evening into the overnight hours across parts of the upper Mississippi Valley.

sections.title: 01Z Outlook Update
sections.text: Even the latest high resolution Rapid Refresh appears to have backed off earlier indications of the possibility of the evolution of a significant cluster of thunderstorms across central Minnesota this evening. This appears consistent with much of the remainder of model output and observational data. Still, increasing thunderstorm development, now ongoing near/north of the Grand Forks area, appears aided by forcing for ascent associated with a low amplitude impulse within a generally zonal and modest belt of mid-latitude westerlies near and just south of the international border area. A relatively focused/concentrated area of enhanced low-level warm advection ahead of a weak surface low could still support further upscale growth this evening. The evolution of a fairly compact mesoscale convective system may not be out of the question, accompanied by a transition to primarily a severe wind threat, with a tendency to propagate southeastward along a remnant zone of stronger differential heating toward the Detroit Lakes and Brainerd areas. The western flank of a significant cold front (trailing westward from the deep mid-level closed low now accelerating eastward across northern Quebec)

sections.title: Northern Maine
sections.text: As suggested by the 00Z sounding from Caribou, instability is weak, and not likely to get any better. However, convection now spreading into the region could still pose some risk for localized strong wind gusts this evening, in the presence of deep layer westerly mean flow increasing to 40-50 kt. ..Kerr.. 07/12/2017

mesoscale_discussions.summary: Isolated strong to severe gusts are possible over the next hour.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: Radar mosaic shows a long-lived MCS located over east-central IL moving east-southeast at 45 kt. Temperatures over west-central IN are steady in the upper 70s degrees F and have been stunted due to cloud cover and an earlier thunderstorm cluster of IN. As a result, destabilization is not expected to increase further. However, measured ASOS gusts of 46-kt at Decatur, IL at 1436Z and 53-kt at Champaign, IL at 1457Z indicate at least some isolated risk for strong to severe gusts may persist in the near term. Once the MCS overtakes a line located from near Crawfordsville to Greencastle, the risk for stronger gusts will probably decrease as rain-cooled outflow detrimentally interacts with the approaching MCS.

mesoscale_discussions.summary: Convective initiation is forecast over the next 1-2 hours. Severe thunderstorms capable of large to very large hail, severe gusts, and possibly a tornado are forecast this evening. A convective watch is likely in the next 1-2 hours.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: Visible satellite imagery shows several areas of clumping/agitated cumulus. Weak low level confluence is implied by streamline analysis across east-central SD near Huron where a cumulus field is present as of 2040Z. Other areas where storm initiation may occur may evolve from where the boundary layer is probably more deeply mixed near the MO River near the SD/ND border and farther north to the north of Jamestown, ND. RAP forecast soundings show a very unstable airmass (3000-4000 J/kg MLCAPE) from east-central SD into east-central ND within a moist axis with upper 60s-lower 70s degrees F dewpoints. Southerly low-level winds veering and increasing with height to 35-kt in the mid levels is resulting in around 40-45 kt effective shear. Once updrafts break the cap, rapid severe storm development is forecast. Large hail will be the initial risk. Hail diameters in excess of 2 inches in diameter are possible with the most intense supercells. A risk for a tornado may develop towards evening dependent on both convective mode and storms moving into an environment near the ND/MN border and over west-central MN where hodographs are slightly larger. Severe gust potential will likely increase as storms congeal this evening.

mesoscale_discussions.summary: At least isolated storms are in the process of developing over eastern South Dakota. These storms will pose a risk for isolated large hail and downburst winds. Some uncertainty still exists regarding overall coverage of severe events and duration of the threat. Trends will continue to be monitored for a possible WW.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: Early this evening satellite trends show towering cumulus and an isolated storm or two developing along a pre-frontal trough that extends across eastern SD. Latest objective analysis shows the atmosphere to be strongly unstable with a corridor of up to 3000 J/kg MLCAPE and 30-40 kt 0-6 km shear supportive of mid-level updraft rotation, and storms will likely intensify as they develop east. The weak low-level flow, weak forcing aloft and onset of nocturnal cooling might limit duration of threat. Nevertheless, this environment will promote a risk for isolated large hail and downburst winds through at least early evening.

mesoscale_discussions.summary: Storms including supercells are expected to continue from eastern North Dakota through northwest Minnesota next couple hours, posing a threat for a few tornadoes, large hail and damaging wind.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: Cluster of supercells that initiated along what appears to be a cold front/dryline merger just south of surface low continues from northeast ND into extreme northwest MN. Surface analysis indicates a warm front extending from northeast ND southeastward through western MN. Greater tornado threat next couple hours is expected with storms that interact with this boundary where low-level shear is maximized. More isolated development remains possible farther south over southeast ND. Overall tornado threat should begin to decrease by 03Z as the boundary layer stabilizes. ..Dial.. 07/12/2017 ...Please see www.spc.noaa.gov for graphic product...

mesoscale_discussions.summary: Storms (a few with some supercell structures) are expected to continue developing northeast through northern IL and southern WI this evening. Primary threat appears to be a few instances of large hail. However, a brief tornado cannot be ruled out. Overall threat does not appear sufficient for a WW but trends will continue to be monitored.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: As of mid evening a cluster of storms has initiated over northeast IA into southern WI and northern IL. Activity is developing in response to a strengthening southwesterly low-level jet which is augmenting isentropic ascent and destabilization near and north of a warm front that stretches from north central IA into northern IL. The 0-1 km Hodograph size will increase further as the low-level jet strengthens, but this will occur with a stabilizing boundary layer which suggests storms should become increasingly elevated. Large hail should remain the primary threat with this activity, but a brief tornado cannot be ruled out before the surface layer decouples.

mesoscale_discussions.summary: Threat for isolated large hail and damaging wind will persist through 04-05Z over eastern South Dakota followed by a general decrease in overall threat. The remaining portion of severe thunderstorm watch 409 is scheduled to expire at 04Z, but can be locally extended in time for an hour or so if needed.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: Thunderstorms that developed earlier along dryline persist over eastern SD. Some supercell structures remain with a threat for large hail. However, activity is primarily diurnally driven, and as the boundary layer cools with surface temperatures falling into the 70s, convective inhibition should increase significantly resulting in a general decrease in storm coverage and intensity. ..Dial.. 07/12/2017 ...Please see www.spc.noaa.gov for graphic product...

mesoscale_discussions.summary: Strong/damaging wind gusts and large hail remain severe-weather threats across WW 410 as storms continue to develop and spread to the east in central and southern MN. A new severe thunderstorm watch is being considered to the east of WW 410 across parts of northern and central WI.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: Time lapse of mosaic radar imagery during the early overnight indicated storms have been clustering across the northern portion of WW 410 in central MN (Douglas County to Kanabec County) and tracking to the east at 35-40 kt. Meanwhile, a smaller cluster of storms was moving east through McLeod County, MN. Additional storms were developing to the north-northeast into west-central WI (Trempealeau to Monroe counties) with rapid cloud-top cooling per IR satellite imagery. Modest southwesterly low-level winds (20-25 kt) across southern MN will continue advect moisture into southern MN and western/central WI with surface dew points in the upper 60s to 70 F. This combined with steep midlevel lapse rates will support additional destabilization (MUCAPE increasing to 2000-3500 J/kg) across WI through 12Z. This thermodynamic improvement is represented in the special 06Z MPX sounding, which also had a 4.2 g/kg increase since 00Z of the mean mixing ratio - now at 17.8 g/kg. Aside from the 00Z Hi-res WRF-ARW and the recent two runs of the HRRR (04Z/05Z), CAMS lack a good representation of ongoing storms across the upper MS Valley. Given a modest low-level jet and westerly flow aloft across the northern tier of the U.S., the potential exists for ongoing storms in central MN to evolve into a forward propagating north-south oriented line of storms, as this activity reaches western WI between 08-09Z. Convective trends will be monitored in the short term, and if bowing segments develop, then a new WW would be needed to the east of WW 410. ..Peters.. 07/12/2017 ...Please see www.spc.noaa.gov for graphic product...

mesoscale_discussions.summary: Fast-moving (45 kt) bowing line of storms located in Barron to Rusk to western Eau Claire counties will affect parts of central WI between 09-12Z, with a new WW being considered.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: Two clusters of storms merged over east-central MN and surged eastward into west-central WI along a moderate instability gradient, producing damaging winds (trees and wires down). This bow will continue to be capable of producing damaging winds into part of central WI between 09-11Z, though a more stable air mass with eastward extent may limit the threat too far east into northeast WI. Otherwise, this bow may tend to turn to the southeast along the instability gradient and decelerate as it moves into ongoing downstream storms.
